To save money for a new laptop, Marcus tutors at two centers: X and Y. He earns $$15$ per hour tutoring at center X and $$25$ per hour tutoring at center Y. In one week, Marcus earned a total of $t$ dollars from tutoring at the two centers. The graph shown represents all possible combinations of numbers of hours Marcus could have tutored at the two centers to earn $t$ dollars. What is the value of $t$?
explanation: Choice B is correct. Marcus earns $$15$ per hour at center X. Therefore, if he tutors $x$ hours at center X, he earns $$15x$ dollars. Marcus earns $$25$ per hour at center Y, so if he tutors $y$ hours at center Y, he earns $$25y$ dollars. The graph represents all possible combinations of hours that produce a total of $t$ dollars, so the equation $15x + 25y = t$ represents the graph, where $t$ is a constant. Substituting any point $(x, y)$ from the graph yields the value of $t$. The point $(10, 0)$ lies on the graph, so substituting $10$ for $x$ and $0$ for $y$ gives $15 \times 10 + 25 \times 0 = t$, or $t = 150$. Similarly, the point $(0, 6)$ lies on the graph, and substituting yields $15 \times 0 + 25 \times 6 = t$, or $t = 150$.
